proposals.defect: BC-07 exempts a level-three API-reference heading only when its text is in `topics`, a set of bare final dotted segments rebuilt inside the check. The renderer names hubs with composition/renderer.py::_table_names (lines 430-447, called at 462, emitted at 481), which returns the shortest dotted suffix that distinguishes a type whenever two verified types share a final segment - required by README_CONTRACT.md row 14 so the name is one a visitor can import. The two are independent models of one thing and drift on exactly the disambiguated names, so BC-07 rejects a heading the contract requires.
proposals.measured: 3D-.NET: of 293 verified types, Aspose.ThreeD.Property and Aspose.ThreeD.Formats.GLTF.Property share the segment 'Property', so _table_names correctly yields 'ThreeD.Property' and 'GLTF.Property'. The plan made Aspose.ThreeD.Property a hub; the renderer emitted '### ThreeD.Property'; BC-07 failed it. Reproducing the check's own expression: line in api_lines = True, 'ThreeD.Property' in topics = False, bare 'Property' in topics = True - the disambiguation is the sole cause.
proposals.blast_radius: Any surface with two same-named types in different namespaces. Within lane F: PDF-.NET 34 collisions, 3D-.NET 2, Email-.NET 0, Slides-.NET 0. Ordinary in large .NET and Java surfaces.
proposals.proposed_shape: BC-07 computes its allowed hub headings with the renderer's own _table_names() over the same (classes, enums) list renderer.py:462 uses, instead of re-deriving a bare-suffix set - the principle already stated at renderer.py:470-471 and reconciliation/dispositions.py:164-166.
proposals.mutation_test: A facts fixture with two verified classes sharing a final segment, one of them a hub: BC-07 passes on the rendered heading, and still fails on a genuinely non-shell heading.
proposals.owner: the primary (shared code; validation/ is not a lane-F path)

proposals.defect: observe() calls publication_probe.probe_publication(...) exactly once, with no retry, and none exists inside the vendored probe (_vendor/aspose_extraction/publication_probe.py carries only a 10-second timeout; no adapter under package_registries/ retries). core/retry.py:40-42 already declares RETRY_POLICIES['package_registry'] = RetryPolicy(max_attempts=3, initial_seconds=1, maximum_seconds=20), and run_with_retry('package_registry', ...) is used at extractors/platforms/python_registry.py:123 - the PYTHON platform's own path. Every other ecosystem reaches its registry through this shared facade and never uses the policy. So python probes three times with backoff and net, java, typescript, go and rust probe once.
proposals.measured: Ten nuget readings in this worktree on 2026-09-11; five could not be read. 3D-.NET facts-only #1 unreadable; #2 found; 3D-.NET composition run unreadable (BC-02 FAIL); Email-.NET facts-only found; Email-.NET composition run unreadable; PDF-.NET facts-only unreadable; Slides-.NET facts-only found; plus three direct httpx requests to the 3D URL giving 1 ConnectTimeout and 2 x HTTP 200 {"versions":["26.1.0"]}. Every package is published - the successful readings prove it.
proposals.consequence: An unreadable probe gives install_command:<eco> polarity UNRESOLVED, which fails BC-02 at EXTRACTING; repairs.json records it unrepairable, 'EXTRACTING is not repairable by revision', so the run cannot seal. Separately it changes the facts digest, and facts feed upstream_dependencies(), so a bundle sealed under the unlucky reading reopens EXTRACTING (bundle/seal.py:179-192).
proposals.proposed_shape: Wrap the probe_publication call in run_with_retry('package_registry', ...), raising RetryableOperationError when the reading comes back unreadable (published is None), exactly as python_registry.py:123 already does.
proposals.mutation_test: A fetch stub that times out once then answers 200 yields published=True; one that always fails still yields published=None, so 'we could not check' never becomes 'we checked and it is false' (section 29.6 E5 preserved, not weakened).
proposals.owner: the primary (shared facade; extractors/surface/ is not a lane-F path)
proposals.priority_note: Of everything this lane measured, this is the one defect that blocks candidates across every non-Python cohort rather than one repository - lanes C (maven), D (go_modules) and F (nuget) all reach their registry through this facade; C++ has no registry and is spared. It is also the cheapest to fix: one wrapper around an already declared policy.

proposals.defect: The four fact_ids arrays - under core_capabilities, api_hubs, material_limitations and deviations - are all typed {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}} with no enum, no maxItems and no maxLength. planning_schema() specialises section_id, link_fact_id, symbol_fact_id and the four example-ID fields with enums built from bounded_records(), and leaves all four fact_ids arrays untouched. This is arrival item 40's class, one stage later than the site 352fd35 fixed.
